newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Sampo sees premiums up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Finnish Sampo sees premiums up in 1997.

text.p: Finnish insurer Vakuutusosakeyhtio Sampo said in a statement on Wednesday it expected domestic premium income to grow in 1997 and it aimed to continue to pay at least a third of profits in dividends.
"Domestic premium income is expected to grow further due to the positive economic development and pricing decisions in the large insurance classes," it said with its 1996 results.
Sampo's 1996 domestic premium income excluding reinsurance rose 2.8 percent and its market share rose to 35.5 percent from 35.4 percent in 1995, it said.
Operating profit rose to 619 million markka ($121.3 million) last year from 319 million in 1995 and overall net premium income was 3.86 billion markka, up from 3.71 billion.
"The pricing decisions aim at a clear improvement of insurance operations' profitability," Sampo said.
"Sampo's steady and positive profit trend and strong solvency are reflected to shareholders through an active dividend policy aiming to pay out at least of third of group profits," it said.
It proposed a 6.00 markka dividend per share, up from 5.00 markka, representing 37 percent of the 16.19 markka 1996 earnings per share.
